questions.solution:
The equilibrium is possible when there is no exchange of matter between system and surroundings.

At equilibrium state the forward and backward processes occur with same rate (speed)

When a system reaches equilibrium at a given temperature, the forward and reverse reactions are occurring at the same rate, and the concentrations (or partial pressures) of the reactants and products no longer change with time. The solubility is function of solubility product, the value of which is constant at a given temperature.

In planar chromatography in particular, the retardation factor Rf is defined as the ratio of the distance travelled by the centre of a spot to the distance travelled by the solvent front. The more polar spot travels slower, and the less polar spot travels faster. Rf values, on the other hand, are directly related to the rate of movement. (C) At a given temperature, intensity vs frequency curve passes through a maximum value.

(D) The maximum of the intensity vs frequency curve is at a higher frequency at higher temperature compared to that at lower temperature.
questions.solution:
A black body is an idealised object that absorbs all the radiation that falls on it and emits radiation over a broad range of frequencies. 

Black bodies emit and absorb energy in the form of electromagnetic radiation.

The frequency distribution of the emitted radiation from a black body depends on its temperature and is given by Planck's law.

At a given temperature, the intensity vs frequency curve for a black body radiation passes through a maximum value. This frequency is known as the peak frequency or the frequency of maximum emission.

At higher temperatures, the peak frequency of the black body radiation shifts towards higher frequencies (shorter wavelengths). This means that the maximum of the intensity vs frequency curve is at a higher frequency at higher temperature compared to that at lower temperature.

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Maximum power is dissipated in a circuit containing an inductor, a capacitor and a resistor connected in series with an AC source, when resonance occurs.

Statement II: Maximum power is dissipated in a circuit containing pure resistor due to zero phase difference between current and voltage.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is false but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is true
Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are true
Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is true but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is false

questions.solution:
The formula for impedance is given by 

Z=R2+XL-XC2

At resonance, XL=XC. So, Zmin=R

Power will be maximum when impedance is minimum. Thus the maximum power occurs in a purely resistive circuit.

Bohr's formula for angular momentum of an electron in an orbit is given by

L2=2h2π=2L

Hence, the change in angular momentum is 

ΔL=2L-L=L

 T1=300 KT2=600 K

questions.q: The energy of an electromagnetic wave contained in a small volume oscillates with
options: Double the frequency of the wave
Half the frequency of the wave
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the energy confined within the electric component of an electromagnetic wave can be written as

uE=12ε0E2dV   ...1

Let's assume that the equation of the electric component is given by

E=E0 sinωt+ϕ   ...2

Substitute the expression for the electric field component from equation (2) into equation (1) and simplify to obtain the expression for the energy confined within the small volume dV.

uE=12ε0E0 sinωt+ϕ2dV= 12ε0E02sin2ωt+ϕdV=14ε0E021-cos2ωt+2ϕ   ...3

From equation (3), it can be concluded that the frequency of oscillation of the energy confined within a small volume is double the frequency of the wave.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Match List I with List II:

  List I   List II
(A) 3 Translational degrees of freedom (I) Monoatomic gases
(B) 3 Translational, 2 rotational degrees of freedoms (II) Polyatomic gases
(C) 3 Translational, 2 rotational and 1 vibrational degrees of freedom (III) Rigid diatomic gases
(D) 3 Translational, 3 rotational and more than one vibrational degrees of freedom (IV) Nonrigid diatomic gases

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The formula for degree of freedom is given by 

f=3N-k

where N is the number of particles, k is the individual relationship in the system.

For a monoatomic gas particle, N=1, k=0. So, f=3

Hence, monoatomic gas has 3 translational degree of freedom.

For a rigid diatomic gas molecule, there are 5 degrees of freedom, 3 translational and 2 rotational. A diatomic gas can have two extra degrees of freedom due to rotation along two independent axes.

A non rigid diatomic molecule has one extra degree of freedom than a rigid one. This is the vibrational degree of freedom. Hence, it has 6 degrees of freedom.

So, a non rigid diatomic gas has 3 translational, 2 rotational and 1 vibrational degrees of freedom.

A polyatomic gas has more than two atoms per molecule. Hence, the total number of degrees of freedom is 3 translational,  3 rotational and more than one vibrational degree of freedom.

Statement I: If the number of turns in the coil of a moving coil galvanometer is doubled then the current sensitivity becomes double.

Statement II: Increasing current sensitivity of a moving coil galvanometer by only increasing the number of turns in the coil will also increase its voltage sensitivity in the same ratio

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is true but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is false
Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is false but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is true
Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are false
Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are true
questions.solution:
For a moving coil galvanometer, 

NiAB=kθ

The current sensitivity is given by 

Si=NABk

So, if N is doubled then, the current sensitivity is also doubled.

The voltage is given by 

V=BNARkθ

The voltage sensitivity is given by

Sv=NABkR

As, N is increased, R also increases. So, the voltage sensitivity does not change as NR remains constant.

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Pressure in a reservoir of water is same at all points at the same level of water.

Statement II: The pressure applied to enclosed water is transmitted in all directions equally.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are false
Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is true but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is false
Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is false but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is true

questions.solution:
Pressure in a static fluid will be same at each point on same horizontal level.

P=P0+ρgh

where P0 is atmospheric pressure.

Pascal's law states that pressure applied to enclosed water is transmitted equally in all directions. Hence, both the statements are true and this is the right option.

The activity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mo>µ</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of the substance is ________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>10</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Bq</mi></math>.
questions.solution:
It is given that 

λ=1.5×10-5 s-1

Number of moles is 1×10-660=10-76

Number of atoms=number of moles ×NA

N0=10-76×6×1023=1016

Hence, at t=0, A=A0=N0λ, the activity can be given by

A=N0λe-λt⇒A=1016×1.5×10-5×1=15×1010 Bq

At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, the position of the particle is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> and it moves along positive <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis. The displacement of particle in time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mo> </mo><mi>sin</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi><mo> </mo><mo>+</mo><mo> </mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>, then the value <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>δ</mi></math> will be
questions.solution:
Given, the instantaneous equation of motion of the particle is

x=A sinωt+δ   ...1

As the particle is moving along positive x-axis, v=dxdt>0.

Substitute 0 for t and A2 for x into equation (1) and solve to calculate the required phase difference.

A2=Asinω×0+δ⇒sinδ=12=sinπ6⇒δ=π6

questions.q: An object is placed at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> in front of a plane mirror. The virtual and erect image is formed by the mirror. Now the mirror is moved by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> towards the stationary object. The distance by which the position of image would be shifted, will be
questions.solution: When an object is placed in front of a plane mirror, object distance is equal to the image distance. In the first case, the image distance will be 12 cm from the mirror. In the next case, as the mirror is moved towards the object, the object distance becomes 8 cm. Hence, image distance will also be 8 cm.

questions.q: Consider two containers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> containing monoatomic gases at the same Pressure <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>P</mi></mfenced></math>, Volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>V</mi></mfenced></math> and Temperature <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>T</mi></mfenced></math>. The gas in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is compressed isothermally to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math> of its original volume while the gas in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> is compressed adiabatically to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math> of its original volume. The ratio of final pressure of gas in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> to that of gas in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is
questions.solution:
In an isothermal process the temperature is constant.

PV=nRT

So, it can be written that 

PV=PAV8⇒PA=8P

In an adiabatic process,

PVγ=constant

γ for monoatomic gas is 53

So, it can be written

PBP=VV853⇒PB=32P

Thus, the ratio of the pressures is 

PBPA=32P8P=4

questions.solution:
The given data is

 I0=32 W m-2

If=3 W m-2

Thus, by substituting the value, we get

If=I02cos2θ×cos290°-θ   ...(i)

⇒3=16cos2θ·sin2θ

⇒cosθ·sinθ=34⇒sin2θ=32⇒θ=30°

questions.solution:
The general equation for a wave can be written as y=Asinωt+kx. Comparing it with the given equation, y=5 sin6t+0.003x,

ω=6 rad s-1, k=0.003 cm-1

Using the equation, v=ωk

v=60.003×102=20 m s-1

r=15 cmm=1 kgv=22 m s-1

w=12mv2+mgh

⇒w=12×1×222+1×10×0.3

⇒w=245 J
